items.title: A K-injective complex of modules over a flat algebra is K-injective over the base
items.author: The Stacks Project Authors
items.work: Stacks Project, chapter more-algebra.tex (More on Algebra)
items.source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file more-algebra.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
items.difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that K-injectivity descends along a flat ring map, and the proof is a 6-line argument that rewrites the defining vanishing condition by adjunction. It identifies the group of homotopy classes of maps into the complex over the base ring with the corresponding group over the target ring after tensoring the source with the target ring, using the tensor-restriction adjunction together with exactness of the base change; the vanishing condition defining K-injectivity on the target therefore pulls back to the base. The two ingredients — the adjunction and the exactness of tensoring with the flat algebra — are exactly what the flatness hypothesis is needed for, and both are displayed.
